alerts.title: TDF-associated creatinine rise in pregnancy
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients initiating TDF. Creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL (eGFR 78) within 10 weeks of starting TDF, representing a ~38% eGFR decline from baseline. TDF is a known cause of renal toxicity including Fanconi syndrome and acute kidney injury. Pregnancy normally increases creatinine clearance, so a rising creatinine during pregnancy is particularly concerning. However, the urinalysis is normal without proteinuria, and phosphate remains normal, arguing against proximal tubular dysfunction. The eGFR decline approaches the 30% threshold for Grade 2 renal toxicity.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat serum creatinine and eGFR promptly. If decline from baseline reaches 30% or more, consider TDF substitution to TAF and evaluate for Fanconi syndrome.

alerts.title: Missing LFTs and no clinician plan documented
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend LFTs and RFTs when TDF toxicity signs arise, and viral load monitoring at 6 months after ART initiation then every 6–12 months. No liver function tests have been recorded despite 10 weeks on TDF/3TC/DTG. The clinician's assessment and plan are entirely blank, with no orders documented for ongoing renal monitoring, LFTs, or follow-up viral load scheduling. This represents both a monitoring gap and a plan deficiency for a pregnant patient on a regimen with known hepatorenal toxicities.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a plan including repeat creatinine/eGFR, LFTs, and schedule 6-month viral load. Address renal trend before it reaches the 30% decline threshold.

alerts.title: Low-level viremia at 89 copies/mL on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines recognize viral load above 200 copies/mL as associated with transmission risk and treatment failure. This patient's VL of 89 copies/mL is below that threshold but indicates incomplete suppression after 10 weeks. DTG-based regimens typically achieve rapid suppression. Low-level viremia may reflect early adherence challenges, baseline resistance, or pharmacokinetic variability in pregnancy. The viral load should be repeated per schedule at 6 months. If it rises above 200 copies/mL, enhanced adherence counseling and repeat testing are indicated.

evidence.recommended_action: Reinforce adherence counseling. Repeat viral load at 6-month mark per guideline schedule. If VL exceeds 200 copies/mL, provide intensive adherence counseling and repeat.
